source_message_verbatim: Introduction Stocks are used to buy a "part" of a company. When entering a stock, you are expecting the stock price to go up because it is a good company. For example, If I am buying a share of Netflix (NFLX) I think it will go up in the future so I can sell it for more than I bought it at. If you bought those shares of Netflix at $100 and they went to $500 a share, you made $400 a share profit. Other than buying to sell the shares in the future, you may as a means of receiving "dividends". Dividends are percentages of revenue from a company that you receive based on the amount of shares you own. So in basic terms, you buy a share in a company you believe has potential to grow so you can sell those shares for a profit later on. Terminology PT - Price Target SL - Stop Loss Scalp - also known as a daytrade. Quickly getting in and out of a stock. Short Swing - buying a stock to hold throughout the day typically an overnight position expecting it to increase over time Long Swing - Buying a stock at a good entry and holding for weeks or months Short Squeeze - A short squeeze occurs when a stock or other asset jumps sharply higher, forcing traders who had bet that its price would fall to buy it in order to forestall even greater losses. Their scramble to buy only adds to the upward pressure on the stock's price. Limit buy - buying at that exact share price and not any higher Market buy/sell order - buying/selling in the open market (don’t do it with penny stocks we trade) use limit buy/sell to get the best spread Reverse split - Company doesn’t meet requirements to stay listed as is on the exchange Tutes - institutions, big brokerages aka hedge funds. “Big money” that can have large impact on a stock HOD - High of the Day Finding Stocks to Buy The hardest part of trading/investing for most people, is finding what stocks to buy. The best way to get some experience in the market is to buy shares of some big companies. I have listed some of them below BIG NAME STOCKS LIST AMZN - Amazon TSLA - Tesla NFLX - Netflix TWTR - Twitter AAPL - Apple SPY - Spyder ETF FB - Facebook A quick pro tip for buying any of these stocks, is to average into positions if longer term rather than fully enter at once. Paper Trading An amazing way to practice stock trading/investing with zero risk is paper trading. Paper trading allows you to buy and sell stocks with fake money, which is amazing for those who are looking to learn with risking any money. You can use the paper trading system in Webull to practice. Stock Market Tips Before entering a trade, make sure of a few things : Have a stop loss and price target set - Make sure to have a point in where you will sell for minimal losses. Make sure to also not get greedy and take profits at some point. Make sure to do adequate research before entering - Never blindly enter a trade without adequate research. Know what you are trading. Always buy the dips, sell the rips - Whenever everyone is panicking because of a price drop, that's when you buy. Buy low, sell high. Do not trade with emotions!!! - This one is important. DO NOT buy a stock at all time high prices because of FOMO , (Fear of missing out). This is how you lose money in the market. Wait for dips and load up. Don't trade with money you can't afford to lose - Never use your rent money to trade as the market is unpredictable. You could make 100k in one day or lose 20k in one day. You never know so trade with money you can afford to lose!
